results.title: freddy Launches the Health Data Server: One Home for All Personal Health Data
results.content:
Most people now hold their health data in several apps: a ring for sleep, a watch for training, a glucose monitor, a gym log, a lab portal. Each app shows its own part. freddy connects these sources once and keeps every value as the source sends it, with no scores and no changes. The user then chooses how to use it: with any AI assistant through one private link, as a full download, or through the Personal API.

freddy connects 20 sources directly, plus more than 180 apps through Apple Health and Health Connect. Direct sources include Garmin, Oura, Polar, Suunto, Withings, Apple Health, Health Connect and Google Health. New: users can add lab results from a lab report through their AI and see them in one table, and the Personal API is open to build on. freddy has more than 20,000 users. [...] freddy stores each value with the unit, time and time zone the source gave. When a source deletes or replaces a record, freddy does the same. The private link works with any client that supports the Model Context Protocol (MCP), such as Claude or ChatGPT. Users can export every stored value as a CSV file, and developers can build on the Personal API and the open-source CLI. Stored data is encrypted at rest, and every AI read is logged.

freddy is CASA certified by an independent security lab. It never sells user data and never uses it to train AI models. When a user deletes their data, freddy deletes it. [...] "Every device and app shows you one dimension of your health: your ring sees your sleep, your watch sees your training, your lab report sees your blood. You need all of it in one place, in full depth and breadth, before you or your AI can reason about the whole picture and make truly informed decisions," said Tom Tomaszewski, founder of freddy.

freddy is available now at freddy.coach and on the App Store and Google Play.

About freddy: freddy is a personal health data server operated by reThrive Labs LLC, Sheridan, Wyoming.

results.title: freddy Launches iPhone and Android Apps for Its Multi-Wearable Health Data Service | Fitt Insider
results.content:
freddy is a hosted service that consolidates a person’s health and training data (sleep, recovery, heart-rate variability, workouts, and continuous glucose) from wearables, rings, CGMs, and training platforms, and exposes it to any AI client that supports the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Users connect their sources once and receive a private URL they add to the AI of their choice, then ask questions about their own data in plain language instead of switching between separate apps and dashboards. [...] freddy is direct-to-consumer: each user connects their own accounts, the service reads their data on their behalf, and access is read-only and revocable. freddy does not train models on user data. Supported sources include Oura, WHOOP, Garmin, Polar, Withings, Dexcom, Suunto, Hevy, Concept2, Intervals.icu, and Ultrahuman, in addition to Apple Health and Health Connect.

Availability

The freddy apps are available now on the App Store and Google Play.

About reThrive Labs LLC

freddy is the health context layer for AI. It connects a person’s wearables, rings, CGMs, and training platforms to Claude, ChatGPT, and other MCP-compatible AI clients so they can ask about their own health and performance data in natural language.

freddy is operated by reThrive Labs LLC, a Wyoming company.
